title: Normative assembly rule reveals fairness in microbial communities
experiments_summary: The study formed 14 distinct 4-species microbial communities by randomly selecting species from a pool of 16 bacterial strains (from University of Helsinki Culture Collection, HAMBI) known to coexist in laboratory microcosms. All possible subcommunities (15 combinations per block) were assembled combinatorially. Pre-cultivation involved reviving frozen glycerol stocks in proteose-peptone-yeast medium for 22 hours, with cell densities adjusted to 2.4×10^7 cells/mL using OD600 measurements calibrated against flow cytometry and CFU counts. Communities were assembled at 6×10^6 cells/mL per community in M9 minimal medium. Growth assays were conducted in 100% R2A liquid medium in 96-well microplates across four antibiotic conditions: control (sterile MQ water), ampicillin (4.24 µg/mL), streptomycin (6.3 µg/mL), and moxifloxacin (0.06 µg/mL), with concentrations based on median IC50 values across the 16-strain pool. OD600 measurements were taken every 10 minutes for 48 hours at 30°C with shaking at 800 RPM on BioTek LogPhase 600 readers. After growth, culture plates were frozen at -20°C for downstream sequencing. Community composition was determined via 16S amplicon sequencing targeting the V3 region, using fusion primers with iTru adapters and combinatorial indices, sequenced on Illumina MiSeq (2×150 bp reads) at the Finnish Functional Genomics Centre. Sequencing data were demultiplexed using cutadapt, paired-end reads merged with NGmerge, filtered with vsearch, and absolute/relative species abundances derived using Rbec software with 16S gene copy number normalization. Community yields were computed by subtracting background OD from control conditions. Shapley values were computed from the measured community yields across all subcommunities using both the standard formula and a recursive formulation. The fair end-distribution was calculated by normalizing non-negative Shapley values. A modified recursive fair assembly rule was applied using observed true species frequencies from biculture and triplet subcommunities as initial conditions to predict full 4-species community compositions. Prediction accuracy was quantified using Euclidean distance (mean squared error) between predicted and observed community compositions. Community diversity was assessed using the Gini-Simpson index, and cosine similarity between fair and true frequency distributions was used to quantify fairness across conditions.
